name: Will Haven
label: Revelation
lede: Four Sacramento friends built a wall of sludge in the Deftones' backyard, got dragged onto their tours, broke up at the Capitol Garage, and have spent twenty years finding out they can't stay away from it.

eras.title: Three bands for three dollars
eras.text: Will Haven came out of a Sacramento band called Sock and a scene built around Thursday nights at the Cattle Club. Their heroes were Neurosis, Deadguy and Sepultura, and the Deftones were watching from down the street.

years.h: Jeff Irwin talks Grady Avenell into singing
years.p: Guitarist Jeff Irwin and Grady Avenell had been friends since they were 12 or 13. Avenell didn't want to sing; Irwin talked him into it, and with Mike Martin and Wayne Morse, Will Haven formed in Sacramento.
years.xp: The band grew out of a group called Sock. The local hub was the Cattle Club, where Thursdays meant three bands for three dollars, and 924 Gilman Street in Berkeley was a drive away. [[Far|e48fa0b9-7e30-4406-aed2-3605854c9e52]], Deftones and Tinfed were the Sacramento bands they measured themselves against.

years.h: A six-song Will Haven demo
years.p: Will Haven's first recording is a six-track demo, released the year the band formed.

years.h: Will Haven's self-titled EP
years.p: The Will Haven EP draws positive reviews and gets the band out of Sacramento.

years.h: Will Haven turn up in the Deftones' Bored video
years.p: Will Haven appear in the video for the [[Deftones|7527f6c2-d762-4b88-b5e2-9244f1e34c46]]' Bored, a Sacramento cameo years before the two bands shared stages across the world.

years.h: El Diablo: Will Haven's tribute to Neurosis
years.p: Will Haven's debut album, on Crisis and Revelation, opens with the six-minute Stick Up Kid and closes on the near-nine-minute ¡Escucha!. The band calls it a homage to [[Neurosis|a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed]].
years.xp: Eric Stenman engineered and mixed it at The Hangar in Sacramento, the room where the next two records were made too. Revelation, the band says, never asked for a single or a change in sound: being on a hardcore label meant nobody told them what to do.

eras.title: The band the Deftones fought for
eras.text: The Deftones had watched Will Haven form, and once they were big enough to choose their openers, they chose them. Tours with Deftones led to Soulfly, Fear Factory and Slipknot, and Will Haven found an especially loud welcome in the UK.

q: They fought for us to go on tour with them.
years.h: Chino Moreno asks Will Haven to tour with the Deftones
years.p: Deftones singer [[Chino Moreno|e61400d1-9434-4abc-ac7a-4f1dad60cfc7]] approaches Jeff Irwin, then 19, about touring together. The Deftones tours open doors to Soulfly, Fear Factory and Slipknot.
years.xp: Wayne Morse says the Deftones went to bat to get Will Haven on those bills. Revelation's own bio also lists opening slots for the [[Beastie Boys|9beb62b2-88db-4cea-801e-162cd344ee53]] and [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]], and tours of California, the East Coast and Europe.

years.src: Wikipedia: WHVN · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: WHVN, Will Haven's heaviest album · REV 79
years.p: Produced by Eric Stenman and the band at The Hangar and The Appliance Shop. Jeff Jaworski of Red Tape sings backing vocals on a song named after him, Jaworski.
years.xp:
Revelation pressed the first vinyl run as 1,517 white copies; Music for Nations released it in the UK. Slopez features a drum circle by Adam Federico.

In 2021 Metal Hammer named WHVN one of the 20 best metal albums of 1999.

years.h: Will Haven cover Bad Brains' The Regulator
years.p: Will Haven's version of [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]]' The Regulator appears on the tribute album Never Give In.

years.h: Mitch Wheeler replaces drummer Wayne Morse
years.p: Founding drummer Wayne Morse leaves Will Haven and Mitch Wheeler takes over the kit.

years.h: Grady Avenell guests on Soulfly's Pain
years.p: Grady Avenell adds vocals to [[Soulfly|832a43c7-aa7d-439b-a6b4-4f1afa671c24]]'s Pain, one of several guest spots that include tracks by [[Far|e48fa0b9-7e30-4406-aed2-3605854c9e52]].

years.h: Carpe Diem · REV 104
years.p: Eric Stenman produces again. In the UK, via Music for Nations, it reaches No. 24 on the Rock & Metal Albums chart, and the title song hits No. 17 on the rock singles chart.
years.xp:
The closer, Moving to Montana, runs almost nine minutes, with a hidden track at 6:15 after twenty seconds of silence. Reviews split hard: Drowned in Sound gave it 9/10, Metal Hammer 5/10.

The tour behind it took Will Haven across the US, the UK and Japan, plus the Australian Warped Tour.

eras.title: The last night at the Capitol Garage
eras.text: After the Carpe Diem tours, Grady Avenell walked away to go back to school and look after his family. Will Haven played one more hometown show and filmed it.

years.h: Grady Avenell quits Will Haven for school and family
years.p: When the Carpe Diem touring ends, Grady Avenell leaves Will Haven to pursue his education and family life.

years.h: Foreign Films: the final show at Sacramento's Capitol Garage
years.p: Will Haven's last show before the split, at the Capitol Garage in Sacramento, comes out on DVD as Foreign Films, a title that echoes the El Diablo song Foreign Film. Then the band goes dark.

eras.title: A revolving door at the microphone
eras.text: Will Haven came back in late 2005 with Grady Avenell, then lost him again in the middle of making the comeback record. For two years the singer was the man they'd named a song after.

years.h: Will Haven reunite, with Grady Avenell back
years.p: Will Haven regroup with Grady Avenell, drummer Mitch Wheeler and new guitarist Cayle Hunter of Ghostride.

q: This is Grady's calling right here.
years.h: Chino Moreno sits in on Will Haven's pre-production
years.p: Deftones singer [[Chino Moreno|e61400d1-9434-4abc-ac7a-4f1dad60cfc7]] works with Will Haven in Los Angeles on the songs for their first album since Carpe Diem. Jeff Irwin is thrilled to hear Grady Avenell sing again.

years.big: The singer they'd named a song after
years.h: Grady Avenell leaves again; Jeff Jaworski takes the mic
years.p: Will Haven make The Hierophant at Bieler Bros. Studios in Pompano Beach, Florida. Then Grady Avenell departs again, and Jeff Jaworski of Red Tape, the namesake of the WHVN song Jaworski, replaces him.
years.xp: The Hierophant came out on Bieler Bros. Records. Jaworski had already sung backing vocals on Will Haven's 1999 album.

years.h: Grady Avenell rejoins for good; benefit shows for Chi Cheng
years.p: Grady Avenell returns to Will Haven permanently. The band plays benefit shows for Deftones bassist [[Chi Cheng|ed1c0daa-9cdb-4bd8-8f46-794ec0783544]].

years.h: Slipknot's Chris Fehn plays bass in Will Haven
years.p: [[Slipknot|a466c2a2-6517-42fb-a160-1087c3bafd9f]] percussionist [[Chris Fehn|2610ba0c-fe94-4e04-8e15-4b29966afffc]] takes over bass in Will Haven, a band Slipknot once toured with. He stays until 2012.

years.h: Voir Dire, on Bieler Bros. and Holy Roar
years.p: Will Haven's fifth album comes out on Bieler Bros. in the US and the UK's Holy Roar.

years.h: Adrien Contreras becomes Will Haven's bassist
years.p: Adrien Contreras replaces Chris Fehn on bass and is still in the band today.

eras.title: Thirty years of WHVN
eras.text: Settled at last, Will Haven made records on their own schedule for Minus Head Records, filmed a sequel to their breakup DVD, and went back out to play Carpe Diem for the people who'd grown up on it.

years.h: Open the Mind to Discomfort EP
years.p: Will Haven's EP comes out on Artery Recordings.

years.h: Muerte, Will Haven's first for Minus Head
years.p: Will Haven's sixth album starts their run on Minus Head Records.

years.h: Foreign Films II, a documentary sequel
years.p: Will Haven release a documentary on regrouping and making Muerte. Jeff Irwin says it has the feel of the original Foreign Films, from a more mature band.

years.h: VII, and the Carpe Diem/VII tour
years.p: Recorded at Pus Cavern in Sacramento with Joe Johnston, partly through the pandemic. Sean Bivins joins on keys and guitar, and an August US tour pairs the new album with Carpe Diem.
years.xp: UK and French dates followed in October 2023.

years.h: No Stars to Guide Me: 30 Years of WHVN
years.p: Will Haven release the single KIRE ahead of a 30th-anniversary compilation on Minus Head.
